method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across counsel as care, words and deeds, kindly attention and correction, trust and justice, strength that refuses harm, learning and understanding, education and particular lives, wisdom and timing, unity, faithful response to revelation, adversity, service and utterance, and the value of time. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: Sow the seeds of love in the heart and not the seeds of hatred.
selected.reason: Reported counsel to sow seeds of love rather than hatred; a brief, memorable image of the inner source of conduct.

selected.text: You must do a little better. The better you do, the better it is.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s brief letter saying you must do a little better, and the better you do, the better it is; a gentle, personal counsel kept in its setting.

selected.text: strive in outward matters according to thy capacity. This is thy duty
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to strive in outward matters according to capacity as a duty; opens the movement on adversity with effort.

selected.text: O leaf! The Tree commands: do not fall short in knowledge, calligraphy and character.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a young woman not fall short in knowledge, calligraphy and character; a concise counsel to a particular recipient.

selected.text: In the acquisition of perfection, negligence is not permissible. Exert thy utmost endeavor.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring negligence impermissible in the acquisition of perfection; a concise call to effort.

selected.text: At most it is that one is ignorant and should be taught, is sick and should be treated, and so on.
selected.reason: Reported words that at most a person is ignorant and should be taught or sick and should be treated; reframes faults as needs.

selected.text: He, verily, enjoineth upon all men what is right, and forbiddeth whatsoever degradeth their station
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Strive thou to attain unto that which shall endure as long as the Kingdom of earth and heaven endureth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to strive for that which endures as long as earth and heaven; a concise statement of lasting deeds.

selected.text: We have counselled all in what shall profit them in the hereafter and in this world. Blessed are they who act!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s brief blessing on those who act upon His counsels for this world and the next; a concise call to practice.

selected.text: Strive that from thee may appear a deed that shall enter and be preserved in the treasury of divine acceptance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to strive for a deed that is preserved in the treasury of divine acceptance; anticipates the guide’s question on lasting deeds.

selected.text: Tell them that if they would attain nearness to the Blessed Beauty they must love much, for love is everything.
selected.reason: Reported words that those who would draw near to the Blessed Beauty must love much, for love is everything; a brief statement of love as the root.

selected.text: O servant, hear My words! By God the Truth, thou shalt not find for thyself a counselor more faithful than I.
selected.reason: Kitab-i-Badi‘ assurance that the servant will find no counsellor more faithful than Bahá’u’lláh; a memorable personal address.

selected.text: Verily My Most Exalted Pen counseleth all who are in the kingdom of creation to observe the Most Great Trustworthiness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to all in creation to observe the Most Great Trustworthiness; states trustworthiness as a universal standard.

selected.text: the clamour of every sinful pretender. O My namesake! Call thou to mind, each day, that whereunto We admonished thee in Our presence. Verily thy Lord, He, in truth, is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding His namesake recall each day the admonitions given in His presence; a narrative trace of personal counsel.

selected.text: O people of Baha! Choose for yourselves a station between slowness and haste. Thus doth command you the Goal of all seekers
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the people of Bahá choose a station between slowness and haste; opens the movement on wisdom and timing.

selected.text: We convey greetings to the women of that land and bid them to sanctification, detachment, supreme chastity and supreme purity.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh greeting the women of a land and bidding them to sanctification, detachment and supreme chastity; counsel addressed to women.

selected.text: May you be of those who have believed and obeyed; may you be of the few that are chosen rather than of the many that are called!
selected.reason: Reported hope that hearers will be of the few chosen rather than the many called; a pointed allusion on response.

selected.text: O thou who hast acquired the light of guidance … Look not at the creatures but rather turn thy gaze to the Creator of creation
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to look not at the creatures but at the Creator; a brief statement of where to fix one’s gaze.

selected.text: You should stay and travel for a time in Zoshto and its surroundings so that, God willing, the blessed tree may take root in that field.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá advising a teacher to stay and travel in Zoshto so that the blessed tree may take root; an example of counsel tied to a journey.

selected.text: Blessed is the soul that ariseth today with complete sincerity and becometh adorned with that which guideth mankind and speaketh thereof.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blessing the soul who arises with sincerity, adorned with what guides mankind, and speaks of it; closes the teaching movement.

selected.text: Hold fast unto the Book, then act according to that which hath been sent down therein from the Pen of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to hold fast to the Book and then act on it; a concise statement of faith joined to practice.

selected.text: Be thou steadfast in thy love, then consort with the people with wisdom and speak unto them with wisdom, for this is a beautiful command.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to consort and speak with people with wisdom; a concise statement of wise association.

selected.text: O people of Baha! Look not upon the creatures and their clamor and oppression, but rather upon the Truth and His justice and sovereignty.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the people of Bahá look not at people’s clamour and oppression but at God’s justice; reorients the reader in adversity.

selected.text: Man must needs possess human qualities. Through God's loving-kindness, all the friends must manifest goodly deeds and spiritual qualities.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh insisting that man must possess human qualities and manifest goodly deeds; a plain statement of the human standard.

selected.text: Fix in thy heart that which the Tongue of Grandeur and Majesty hath spoken, then make mention of it and be not of them that remain silent.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to fix His words in the heart, then mention them and not remain silent; links inner reception and speech.

selected.text: all the friends through distinguished services, and wilt, at all times, arise as an obedient servant to render service to the loved ones of God, for service to the loved ones of God is service to God. Glory be upon all who stand firm in
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: It was beautiful to see how 'Abdu'l-Baha did not emphatically deny their assertions, but gave to understand that much of it was imagination.
selected.reason: Reported account of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá not emphatically denying visitors’ assertions while conveying that much was imagination; a narrative example of tactful correction.

selected.text: O thou who art firm in the Covenant! Now is the time for you to gird up the loins of endeavor and uproot this discord from among the friends.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling a steadfast believer to gird up the loins of endeavour and uproot discord among the friends; a direct charge to reconcile.

selected.text: Today the hosts which bear the standards of triumph and the banners of victory have been and continue to be goodly deeds and pleasing character.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that the hosts of triumph today are goodly deeds and pleasing character; returns to victory through character at the close.

selected.text: O handmaidens of God! Strive that ye may become the source of goodly deeds and that your mention may endure through the Most Great Remembrance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the handmaidens become the source of goodly deeds so that their mention may endure; joins women’s service and lasting deeds.

selected.text: Is there any greater desire than this? It is a big desire. This desire cannot be compared to all others. It is hard to be steadfast, to follow the straight path -- there is nothing harder. There are many who take ten steps in
selected.reason: Reported reply that nothing is harder than remaining steadfast on the straight path; a frank qualification about steadfastness.

selected.text: The relatives, both men and women, must not delay for an instant in acquiring perfection. Thus have We counseled before and in this Manifest Tablet.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding relatives, men and women, not delay an instant in acquiring perfection; counsel to a family.

selected.text: The greatness of the teachings of Baha'u'llah will be known when they are acted upon and practiced. Not one of a hundred has as yet come into force.
selected.reason: Reported words that the greatness of Bahá’u’lláh’s teachings will be known when they are practised; a frank measure of how far practice lags behind profession.

selected.text: O people of Baha! Turn ye with all your being unto God and arise to serve the Cause with such strength of heart and resolve as to shake the mountains.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the people of Bahá serve with strength of heart and resolve to shake the mountains; a vivid call to service.

selected.text: However, all must observe the divine ordinances. By My life! They will benefit you and will bring you to a station that cannot be described in words.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh swearing that the divine ordinances will bring their observers to a station beyond words; affirms the benefit of obedience.

selected.text: Therein doth God command you to practice righteousness and piety, and forbiddeth you from transgression and indecency, would that ye might understand.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that God commands righteousness and piety and forbids transgression and indecency; a plain summary of the moral law.

selected.text: Strive to have noble thoughts and sublime aspirations; endeavour to raise the minds of people and release them from this darkness of blind imitation.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to cultivate noble thoughts and release people from blind imitation; opens the inquiry into learning.

selected.text: Say not unto anyone that which thou wouldst not wish to hear from another, and desire not for any soul that which thou wouldst not desire for thyself.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to say nothing one would not wish to hear and desire for no soul what one would not desire for oneself; carries the guide’s theme of reciprocity.

selected.text: The friends of God must regard creation with the eye of loving-kindness and draw all to the horizon of guidance through kind counsels and goodly deeds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends regard creation with loving-kindness and draw all to guidance through kind counsels and deeds; defines the manner of counsel.

selected.text: Therefore the friends must supplicate to the Abha Kingdom and seek confirmation and success for Abdul-Baha, for the being is weak and the burden is heavy.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking the friends to pray for his confirmation since the being is weak and the burden heavy; a striking example of humility under burden.

selected.text: Let thy mind be alert, thy heart alive. Be like a tidal wave in the sea of God's love that thou mayest cast ashore the pearls of truth and inner significance.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to keep mind alert and heart alive, like a tidal wave casting ashore pearls of truth; a memorable image of learning.

selected.text: In all circumstances, keep thine eye upon wisdom. This is among the binding counsels of God which hath flowed from the Most Exalted Pen in most of the Tablets.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh naming constant attention to wisdom among the binding counsels revealed in most of His Tablets; affirms the weight of wisdom.

selected.text: The friends of God must gird up their loins to serve and become the cause of fellowship and unity of hearts and souls, and in all conditions be mindful of wisdom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends serve as the cause of fellowship and unity of hearts while mindful of wisdom; joins unity and wisdom.

selected.text: When I love people I do not tell them to their faces. You know how much I love Mirza-Abul-Fazl and Haji-Mirza-Heydar-Ali, but I have seldom told them to their faces.
selected.reason: Reported words that ‘Abdu’l-Bahá seldom tells those he loves of it to their faces, naming two devoted believers; a distinctive narrative example of reticent love.

selected.text: Take the cup of utterance from the hand of the bounty of thy Lord, the All-Merciful, then drink therefrom by this Name whereby the pillars of all lands have trembled.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient take the cup of utterance and drink by the Name that made all lands tremble; an image of receiving the Word.

selected.text: Know the value of this Day and occupy yourselves with service, that there might appear from you that which will endure through the eternity of My names and attributes.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends know the value of this Day and serve so that what endures may appear; joins time and service.

selected.text: Fear God and pervert not the Word from its place … Have mercy on yourselves and break not God's covenant and testament. This is sincere counsel, were you but hearing
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh warning against perverting the Word and breaking God’s covenant, calling this sincere counsel; a statement of fidelity.

selected.text: Let not the might of the world frighten thee, nor the utterances of any deluded one cause thee grief. Hold fast unto God in all conditions and cling to His luminous hem.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel not to be frightened by the world’s might or grieved by any deluded one; a direct consolation.

selected.text: Draw them through the influence of Thine utterances unto the Dawning-Place of Thine inspiration, and to the Fountain of Thy Revelation, and to the Treasury of Thy wisdom.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Whatever a man's tongue speaketh, that let him prove by his deeds. If he claimeth to be a believer, then let him act in accordance with the precepts of the Abha Kingdom.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: O servants! We have previously stated that ye are all the fruits of one tree and the leaves of one branch. In the station of love and kindness be as rain-laden clouds
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recalling that all are fruits of one tree and bidding them be as rain-laden clouds in love; a classic image of unity and kindness.

selected.text: Hold fast with complete determination, lest diverse winds prevent thee. In all conditions, keep thy gaze fixed upon the Truth and remain detached and free from aught else.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to hold fast with determination lest diverse winds prevent, keeping the gaze on the Truth; an image of steadiness.

selected.text: Choose ye for yourselves what God hath chosen for you … Rejoice ye in My remembrance of you and arise to that which profiteth you in the world to come and in this first life
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to choose what God has chosen and arise to what profits in both worlds; joins surrender and action.

selected.text: Raise thou this call as much as thou canst, and sound and blow this clarion continually night and day, so that the souls may become quickened and the people find eternal life.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to sound the clarion night and day so that souls may be quickened; an image of proclamation.

selected.text: O servants! Let not your station slip from your grasp. Know your worth and the worth of these days, and drink of the choice-sealed wine in the name of the Self-Subsisting.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the servants know their worth and the worth of these days; a concise call to value time and station.

selected.text: God willing, ye must be the dawning-places of divine counsels among mankind, that through your advice the heedless may turn to the ocean of certitude and the manifest horizon.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh hoping the friends will be dawning-places of divine counsels through whose advice the heedless turn to certitude; describes the giving of counsel.

selected.text: We counsel all to perform pure and holy deeds and to fear God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy. One pure deed amongst the deeds of former centuries is as the sun amongst the stars.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh likening one pure deed among the deeds of former centuries to the sun among the stars; a memorable image of the worth of deeds.

selected.text: O leaf! Great is this Day and mighty is this Cause. You must at all times turn to the All-Merciful in such wise that the intimations of deluded souls will not cause you to slip.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a woman turn always to the All-Merciful so that deluded souls cannot make her slip; counsel to a particular believer in trial.

selected.text: Show ye an effort!  Work unceasingly.  Labor diligently;- so that the everlasting Bounty be realized, Eternal life be destined and the nostrils be perfumed with the holy Fragrances
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to show an effort, work unceasingly and labour diligently; a direct statement of sustained effort.

selected.text: In brief, the hope of 'Abdu'l-Baha is this: that the descendents will bring glory to their predecessors, and that the sons will cause the garden of their fathers' hopes to flourish.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping that descendants will bring glory to their predecessors and make their fathers’ garden of hopes flourish; counsel within families.

selected.text: And if there are any weak ones among the believers, deal with them gently and give counsel - do not be harsh, for harshness causes intensity and obstinacy. Leave them to themselves.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá warning that harshness toward the weak causes obstinacy and bidding the friends leave them to themselves; a necessary qualification on correction.

selected.text: We verily counseled the people aforetime through God's tender mercy, grace, compassion and justice, that every soul might adopt the character of their Lord, the Mighty, the Bountiful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling every soul to adopt the character of their Lord through mercy, grace, compassion and justice; grounds conduct in divine attributes.

selected.text: day and by night; so that ye may conduct yourselves in accord with the Divine Teachings; grant salubrious water to the thirsty ones and be the balm of heart and the healing of the spirit to the sick ones in both worlds
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding the friends give water to the thirsty and be the balm and healing of the sick in both worlds; images of mutual service.

selected.text: If they cannot arrange to go every Sunday, they must go every other Sunday, if not every other Sunday then once a month. But they must come together and must keep up the Sunday School.
selected.reason: Reported insistence that a Sunday School be kept up even if only monthly; a concrete instance of practical persistence.

selected.text: Strive that from the trees of existence such fruits may appear and become manifest as befit the station of man. This is the counsel of the Peerless Friend unto thee and unto His friends
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel that the trees of existence should bear fruits befitting the station of man; an image of character as fruit.

selected.text: Hold thou fast unto the cord of steadfastness in such wise that neither the affairs of men nor the veils of those who have disbelieved in God, the Mighty, the Beloved, may disturb thee.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient hold so fast to steadfastness that neither men’s affairs nor the veils of disbelievers disturb him; a clear statement of firmness.

selected.text: Grieve not at the thoughts of the deniers in your presence, but rely upon God, your Lord. Verily He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing in truth, and your Lord has power over all things.
selected.reason: The Báb’s counsel not to grieve at the thoughts of deniers but rely upon God; adds the Báb’s counsel of reliance.

selected.text: Take ye, O My loved ones, the bounds and ordinances of God. Beware lest the intimations of such as have been heedless of God through following the promptings of self and desire debar you.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the loved ones take the bounds and ordinances of God and not be debarred by those who follow self and desire; joins law and inner freedom.

selected.text: At all times be engaged in the remembrance of the All-Merciful and summon the people to the direction of the All-Glorious. This is the fruit of human existence in this time and all times.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling remembrance and summoning people to God the fruit of human existence in all times; a statement of life’s purpose.

selected.text: this Wronged One hath at all times enjoined upon the peoples of the earth in general such counsels and wisdom as would extinguish the fire of hatred and sedition, conflict and corruption
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that He has always enjoined counsels that extinguish the fire of hatred, sedition and conflict; summarises the purpose of His counsels.

selected.text: You are the children of the new time. Your thoughts should always be as to how you may become wise and good. You should seek sagacity and prudence, and to make progress in the right path.
selected.reason: Reported words to the ‘Akka schoolboys that the children of the new time should think how to become wise and good; places counsel in a school setting.

selected.text: Therefore immerse yourself in this vast, surging ocean, soar in this lofty, ascending height, sing with the most wondrous melodies in this verdant garden, and hold fast to this firm cord.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to immerse oneself in the surging ocean, soar to the height and sing in the verdant garden; vivid imagery of receptivity.

selected.text: Beware lest ye commit that which would cause sedition. Be united in the Cause and be not of those who differ … Beware lest ye differ in God's Cause and follow the imaginings of the doubters
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh warning against sedition and difference in the Cause and following the imaginings of doubters; a warning that guards unity.

selected.text: O servants! Practice truthfulness, turn not away from the destitute, make mention of Me before the great ones, and fear not. … O servants! Be pure in your deeds and follow the word of your Lord
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: This Prisoner counseleth all to perform such deeds as shed abroad the fragrance of sincerity. Work ye according to that which ye have been commanded in the Book of God, the Lord of all worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling deeds that shed the fragrance of sincerity; links action with inner purity.

selected.text: Beware lest anything prevent thee from the remembrance of thy Lord. Leave behind what is with the people and take hold of this Book through a power from thy Lord, the Mighty, the All-Bountiful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient let nothing prevent remembrance and take hold of the Book through God’s power; joins remembrance and fidelity.

selected.text: Strive, O people, that your names may be mentioned before the Throne and there may appear from you that whereby your remembrance shall endure through the eternity of God, the Lord of existence.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: O people! Fear God, shed not blood, oppose no soul, and be of the doers of good. Beware lest ye spread corruption in the land after its reformation, and follow not the ways of the heedless.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s command to shed no blood, oppose no soul and be of the doers of good; an early statement of the refusal of violence.

selected.text: When you consider the end results of things, reality will become evident and the outcome clear and manifest. In matters one must not look at the beginning - consideration of the end is necessary.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to consider the end of matters rather than their beginning; carries the guide’s question on the end of a matter.

selected.text: However, the cause of success and prosperity is trustworthiness and religiosity and effort and zeal, and conduct and movement according to divine teachings. Strive in your work but trust in God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá naming trustworthiness, religiosity and effort as the cause of success and urging work with trust in God; applies trust to ordinary work.

selected.text: Occupy thyself with the Kingdom as much as thou canst and forget all else save the True One; in order that thou mayest, day by day, find a new power in the Cause of God and gain a great stability.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to occupy oneself with the Kingdom so as to find new power and stability day by day; links devotion and steadfastness.

selected.text: We counsel you to observe that which We have revealed in the Book. Hold fast unto it and be not of the heedless ones. Cast behind you the tales of old and cleave unto this Most Great Announcement.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the people cast behind them the tales of old and cleave to the Most Great Announcement; a call to new response.

selected.text: O Hasan! Beseech thou the True One to enable thee to build an edifice, whose foundation shall be piety, whose walls shall be divine confirmations, and whose roof shall be fidelity and truthfulness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of an edifice founded on piety, walled by confirmations and roofed with fidelity and truthfulness; opens the movement on trust.

selected.text: With every group, even if it be an oppressive party, they must act with the utmost trustworthiness, religiosity and kindness. This is the path of the Baha'is, this is the way of the spiritual ones.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá requiring trustworthiness and kindness even toward an oppressive party; a demanding application of goodwill.

selected.text: this most exalted station. We counsel thee with that which will cause the elevation of thy station. The world is transient - look not unto it, but rather unto Him Who created and manifested it. This Wronged One hath ever enjoined upon His servants that which is conducive to the appearance of divine bounty and blessing
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling the world transient and bidding the recipient look to its Creator; a clear statement of detachment.

selected.text: My admonition to you is this. Be thoughtful of attaining to that which was the utmost desire of the Saints. Strive with all your heart and soul to attain to the Kingdom of God. This is my wish for you.
selected.reason: Reported admonition to Emma Blum to strive with heart and soul for the Kingdom, the utmost desire of the saints; a personal counsel.

selected.text: Keep the counsels of the Wronged One before your eyes, for whatsoever has been and is spoken is and shall be pure good. Hold fast to the Sure Handle and cling to the hem of the grace of the Lord of Names
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient keep His counsels before his eyes, for whatever He has spoken is pure good; affirms the worth of counsel.

selected.text: We counsel thee to remember God and praise Him in thy days. The world and all that thou beholdest today shall pass away, but there shall endure for thee what hath flowed from My Most Exalted Pen in thy name
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh assuring a recipient that the world will pass but what His Pen has revealed in his name will endure; a memorable statement of what lasts.

selected.text: Today one must aid the Cause of God through the hosts of spiritual virtues, goodly words, and deeds that are pleasing and acceptable. These hosts are and have ever been mightier than the hosts of the world.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling spiritual virtues, goodly words and pleasing deeds the hosts that aid the Cause, mightier than the hosts of the world; a key image of moral strength.

selected.text: Under all conditions, hold fast to the cord of mercy and regard all with grace. Ye are the flowing rivers that branch from the Most Great Ocean; ye must sacrifice yourselves for the advancement of the world.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling the friends flowing rivers from the Most Great Ocean who must sacrifice themselves for the world’s advancement; a vivid image of merciful service.

selected.text: that thy purpose may be that which God hath purposed for thee, for that which He hath purposed should be the purpose of every soul. Choose not for thyself save that which He hath chosen for thee and commanded thee, for He is the Unconstrained, and hath chosen what His righteous servants, they that are among the most virtuous, have
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel that one’s purpose should be what God has purposed and one should choose only what He has chosen; a substantive teaching on surrender of will.

selected.text: It is incumbent upon all the friends of God to protect these helpless people lest they become again afflicted with the vain imaginings of the former party and remain deprived of the recognition of the Purpose.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh making it incumbent on the friends to protect helpless people from the vain imaginings of a former party; joins fidelity and protection.

selected.text: Strive, O people of the world, that there may be sent down from the Supreme Pen that which shall preserve your names, your spirits and your stations in a Book which none hath known save God, the Lord of Lords.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the people of the world strive that their names and stations be preserved in a Book known only to God; an image of what endures.

selected.text: My object in taking that long journey through the West- was to awaken them out of this sleep; that they may not grovel all the time in the world of matter and that they may not only think of eating and drinking
selected.reason: Reported words that the long journey through the West was meant to awaken people from absorption in matter; a narrative example of counsel carried abroad.

selected.text: We counsel all to love, mercy and fellowship. Verily He is the Lord of creation, the Merciful to His servants, the Protector of lands. There is none other God but He, the Commander in the beginning and in the end.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling all to love, mercy and fellowship; a plain statement of the spirit of kindly attention.

selected.text: It biddeth the people to observe justice and to work righteousness, and forbiddeth them to follow their corrupt inclinations and carnal desires, if perchance the children of men might be roused from their slumber.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: The loved ones of God must appear before all people adorned with the ornament of trustworthiness, truthfulness and purity, and must strive with all their might to foster the unity of hearts and fellowship of souls
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the loved ones appear adorned with trustworthiness, truthfulness and purity and foster the unity of hearts; links integrity with fellowship.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient spread the divine verses with striving, wisdom and utterance, promising assistance; a clear teaching counsel.

selected.text: Stand firm in that land and reform the deeds of those who spread corruption therein while claiming "We are the reformers … O Yahya, recite unto him what God hath permitted thee and kindle him with thy Lord's fire
selected.reason: The Báb bidding a recipient stand firm and reform the deeds of corrupters who claim to be reformers; adds the Báb’s voice to the call to firmness.

selected.text: You must at all times call every soul to forbearance and calm and encourage them to tread the path of godly character and spiritual truths, and inspire them to walk in the footsteps of the martyr in the path of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding a believer call every soul to forbearance and calm and to godly character; describes counsel toward calm.

selected.text: O chosen one! Among all the servants, thou wert the first to attain unto God Himself and to believe in His presence. Stand thou firm in the Cause in such wise that through thy steadfastness all may become steadfast.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the first to believe stand firm so that through his steadfastness all may become steadfast; a narrative example of exemplary firmness.

selected.text: Be thou articulate in His remembrance and steadfast in His service in such wise that neither the veils of the world nor the allusions of them who have disbelieved in God, the Mighty, the Loving, shall hold thee back.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient be articulate in remembrance and steadfast in service despite the veils of the world; joins speech and service.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping a believer’s steadfastness will make every wavering one firm; shows firmness as service to others.

selected.text: Beware lest the veils of the world and its manifestations and colors prevent you. Arise to promote the Cause with complete dedication and great steadfastness, and summon humanity unto truth through wisdom and utterance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to arise with dedication and steadfastness and summon humanity through wisdom and utterance; a concise call to teach.

selected.text: He counseleth all to such deeds, actions and utterances as will cause the exaltation of God's Cause, and whose very performance will testify to their sanctity and detachment from whatsoever is contrary to the Book of God
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling deeds and utterances whose very performance testifies to sanctity and detachment; shows conduct as its own evidence.

selected.text: We command them to unity and love and to that which God hath revealed in the Book. In this case they will surely witness that which will bring forth joy and gladness and delight and exultation, and all will be made happy.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh promising joy and gladness to those who heed His command to unity and love; shows the fruit of unity.

selected.text: We counsel thee and My loved ones in that land to be patient and forbearing, and to manifest that whereby the signs of justice may be revealed amongst the servants. Verily, thy Lord is the All-Patient, the All-Forbearing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling patience and forbearance and the manifestation of justice; links restraint with justice.

selected.text: Be luminous, so that you may bestow eternal illumination upon the world of humanity and dispel the sorrowful darkness of humankind. May you become a light from the Supreme Horizon and a radiant beam from the Abha Kingdom.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to be luminous and dispel the sorrowful darkness of humankind; an image of service as light.

selected.text: Therefore, guide everyone day and night to that which brings comfort to 'Abdu'l-Baha's heart, and lead them through blessed character and conduct. Be a divine counselor and guide to the path of spiritual joy and delight.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding a believer be a divine counsellor who leads through blessed character and conduct; describes counsel as a role.

selected.text: O friends! A time will come when I shall depart from among you. I have done what needed to be done. To the extent of my strength, I have served the Cause of Baha'u'llah. Day and night throughout my life I have not rested.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that a time will come when he departs, having served day and night without rest; a closing example of a life of service.

selected.text: O son of Abhar! Look not at the people and their deeds, neither be thou grieved by their derision, their words and their actions. Fix thy gaze upon the Most Sublime Horizon, and voice His praise in the kingdom of creation.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling the son of Abhar not to grieve at derision but to fix his gaze on the Most Sublime Horizon; models steadiness under criticism.

selected.text: We have counseled all to be trustworthy, truthful and faithful, and to manifest those qualities through which the Cause of God was revealed in former ages. Blessed is he who hath heard and acted, and woe unto the heedless.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recalling His counsel to be trustworthy and truthful and blessing those who heard and acted; joins trust and practice.

selected.text: Pay no attention - stay focused on your work. … Hold general meetings in your home and give eloquent talks with complete courage, and be assured that the breaths of the Holy Spirit will assist you and you will be victorious
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding a believer pay no attention to opposition, stay focused on work and hold meetings with courage; practical counsel for teaching.

selected.text: Thou must needs hold fast to such goodly deeds and praiseworthy character that their fragrance shall be diffused. In all conditions God hath confirmed and will confirm thee. … Be thou assured and be of those who are steadfast
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to hold fast to deeds and character whose fragrance is diffused, with assurance of confirmation; a promise attached to conduct.

selected.text: We counsel thee to be steadfast in this Cause, for through it the feet of them that have attained have slipped. Turn not unto the world and its affairs. In all matters place thy trust in God, the Single One, the All-Informed.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling steadfastness in a Cause through which even those who attained have slipped, and trust in God; a necessary warning.

selected.text: Be thou steadfast in the Cause in such wise that the sincere ones may find in thee that which beseemeth the days of thy Lord, the All-Knowing. Preserve this most exalted station through the name of thy Lord, the Most Glorious.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient be so steadfast that the sincere find in him what befits the days of God; shows firmness as example.

selected.text: Therefore must the loved ones of God carry out His commandments with the utmost joy and fragrance, and shun that which He hath forbidden. This is the supreme counsel that hath issued forth from the Pen of the Lord of eternity.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends carry out His commandments with utmost joy and fragrance; joins obedience and joy.

selected.text: I swear by the Light of the world that any deed performed in these days for the sake of God shall be reckoned among the most excellent of deeds. Strive that ye may attain unto that which befitteth and beseemeth the Days of God.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh swearing that any deed done for God in these days is among the most excellent; affirms the worth of present action.

selected.text: All are commanded today to observe wisdom, and this firm divine decree hath been revealed in most of the Tablets, for lack of wisdom hath been and shall be the cause of commotion among the people and the perturbation of souls.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that lack of wisdom has been and will be the cause of commotion and perturbation; explains why wisdom is commanded.

selected.text: That which is necessary today has been and will be to act according to the divine ordinances. One must summon the people to the highest horizon with the utmost wisdom and to act according to what hath been sent down in the Book.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that what is needed today is to act on the divine ordinances and summon the people with utmost wisdom; joins practice and wise teaching.

selected.text: Ponder, O people, then read what We have sent down in truth. Verily it guideth you unto My Straight Path. Hold fast unto the cord of your Lord's loving-kindness and abandon that which ye were commanded by every ignorant doubter.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to ponder and then read what He has sent down, holding to loving-kindness rather than every doubter; ties reflection to guidance.

selected.text: Remind the people of this announcement which hath been sent down in the Tablets. Say: O people! When ye hear the call of the Calf, leave it behind you. This is what God hath counseled you, for verily He is witness to all things.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the people leave behind the call of the Calf when they hear it; a memorable image of discernment.

selected.text: Therefore I hope that you will arise to exalt the Word of God, for today the hosts of divine confirmation and success are rushing forth and awaiting the arising of sincere souls. Whoever arises will be victorious and triumphant.
selected.reason: Reported Paris words that the hosts of confirmation await the arising of sincere souls and whoever arises will triumph; a call to outward service.

selected.text: We counsel you to fear God and to that whereby His Cause is exalted amongst the servants. Consort with all people with spirit and fragrance, and remind them with wisdom of that which will profit them in the beginning and the end.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to consort with all with spirit and fragrance and remind them with wisdom; joins fellowship and wise reminder.

selected.text: I counsel thee to be patient and tranquil, and to observe that which God hath revealed in His Book. Circle round the will of My Afnan, upon whom be My glory and My mercy and My loving-kindness, then follow what he commandeth thee.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling patience and tranquillity and following the will of His Afnan; counsel within a particular relationship.

selected.text: Continue attending to affairs with the utmost joy, delight and greatest gladness. We beseech God to assist you in completing your tasks. You have truly undergone hardship, but arise to set matters right with perfect steadfastness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh encouraging a recipient who has undergone hardship to continue his tasks with joy and set matters right; counsel for particular circumstances.

selected.text: The first thing incumbent upon the friends of God is to purify their hearts from rancor and hatred, to sanctify and cleanse themselves from bestial qualities, and to act upon the divine ordinances with the utmost joy and fragrance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh naming the first duty of the friends as purifying hearts from rancour and hatred and acting on the ordinances with joy; a foundational statement.

selected.text: O ye heedless ones, become mindful! O ye sleeping ones, be awakened! O ye blind ones, become seeing! O ye deaf ones, become hearing! O ye dumb ones, become speakers! O ye dead ones, become living! O ye deprived ones, take a portion!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s cascade of calls to the heedless, sleeping, blind and deaf to awaken; a vivid summons to hear.

selected.text: O people! Follow not your vain imaginings, nor take the property of others wrongfully, nor dispute with anyone … Be emblems of guidance among all creatures and manifestations of the favors of your Lord, the Kind, the Merciful
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh forbidding wrongful taking of property and disputation and bidding the people be emblems of guidance; joins honesty and example.

selected.text: We bid thee deal with kindness towards his family and with justice and equity in all matters. We have counseled thee and them that believe in Tablets numerous with that which shall cause the Cause of God to be exalted above all else
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient deal with kindness toward a family and with justice and equity in all matters; a practical application of kindly attention.

selected.text: We counsel all to observe that which hath been revealed in the Book of God. Whoso acteth in accordance therewith in this Day is reckoned among the people of Baha. Say: It behooveth you to observe goodly deeds, and again goodly deeds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counting whoever acts on the Book as among the people of Bahá and urging goodly deeds, and again goodly deeds; an emphatic counsel to practice.

selected.text: I counsel thee to fear God Who created thee by His command and made thee to be of the guided ones. Be patient in all that hath befallen Us and be not dismayed by anything. Therefore, be patient in thyself and be of the patient ones
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient be patient in all that has befallen Him and not be dismayed; ties patience to His own example.

selected.text: The souls who have accepted must hold fast to the divine Tablets and act according to whatsoever hath flowed from the Most Exalted Pen in the Most Holy Book. This is a bounty whereunto nothing in the heavens and earth can be compared.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling the acting upon the Most Holy Book a bounty beyond compare; links obedience with grace.

selected.text: Fix your gaze upon the Most Exalted Horizon and turn unto the Source of His Cause. … Today, goodly words and righteous deeds are the manifestors and revealers of His Cause. Blessed is he who holdeth fast unto them. Woe unto the heedless
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh naming goodly words and righteous deeds the revealers of His Cause today; joins speech and deed as testimony.

selected.text: Be as standards upon the hills among the servants - this behooveth you, did ye but know. Be horizons of guidance among all creatures, such that all may receive blessings from your breaths and be illumined by the lamp of your utterance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends be standards upon the hills and horizons of guidance by whose breaths all are illumined; a vivid image of influence.

selected.text: Those souls who today are sheltered beneath the shade of the Divine Word must first consider in all matters what benefits the Cause of God, and then attend to their own interests, so that the foundation may be established firm and solid.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to consider first what benefits the Cause and then one’s own interests; a practical ordering of responsibilities.

selected.text: Be thou speaking in My praise, gazing toward My horizon, turning unto My face, and standing firm in the service of My wondrous Cause. We have counseled thee with that which shall be a lamp unto thee in the worlds of thy Lord.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing His counsel as a lamp for the recipient in the worlds of God; an image of what counsel provides.

selected.text: At all times one should consider positive possibilities in matters and attribute good intentions, or hidden obstacles. When this is one's approach, peace of mind and tranquility of conscience result; otherwise one is constantly tormented.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to consider positive possibilities and attribute good intentions or hidden obstacles, yielding peace of mind; opens the movement on kindly attention.

selected.text: We counsel thee and those who have believed to show forth such steadfastness as will cause the heaven of idle fancies to be cleft asunder, the earth of vain imaginings to be split open, and the mountain of the people's conceit to crumble.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling a steadfastness that cleaves the heaven of idle fancies and crumbles the mountain of conceit; a vivid image of firmness.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient stand firm and remind the people with wisdom and utterance; a clear statement of the manner of teaching.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that the purpose of the Books is the guidance of mankind and blessing those who understand and act; links understanding and practice.

selected.text: Strive as much as thou canst to manifest thyself in the world of existence and the realm of visibility with the utmost spiritual freshness, inner delicacy and luminous vigor, and to be stirred by the breezes from the garden of the Covenant.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to appear in the world with spiritual freshness, inner delicacy and luminous vigour; an image of outward expression.

selected.text: Today is the day of pure deeds, and deeds are the witness and testimony to words. Words without deeds were never and are not worthy of mention. We beseech God to aid all to perform deeds whose fragrance shall never be cut off from the world.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring today the day of pure deeds, with deeds the witness to words; a foundational statement of the words-and-deeds theme.

selected.text: At all times ye must remind the people of that city of the divine verses with perfect wisdom, that perchance the darkness of the vain imaginings of heedless souls may not prevent the friends from the splendors of the rays of the Sun of Truth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends remind a city of the verses with perfect wisdom; applies wisdom to teaching in a particular place.

selected.text: O party of God! Fear God and follow not your desires. Follow what hath been sent down from the heaven of Command in My perspicuous Book. We have counseled you, and do counsel you, with that which will exalt the Cause of God and your stations.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the party of God follow His Book rather than their desires; a clear statement of faithful response.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating there is no success except through acting on divine counsels, which will revive Iran only if practised; ties counsel to social renewal.

selected.text: We counsel thee to be steadfast and God-fearing in the Cause of God, the Lord of all mankind. Beware lest anything whatsoever debar thee from the Lord of Names or cause thee to tremble at the might of those who have denied the Day of Judgment.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling steadfastness and not trembling at the might of deniers; a clear statement of courage.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding His leaves and handmaidens guard the pearls of divine love in their hearts from thieves and robbers; a memorable image addressed to women.

selected.text: O maidservant of God! I hope that through the grace and bounty of the Intended Lord and the Sovereign of the unseen and seen, He will raise up women who will be manifest signs of this Most Great Revelation and evident standards among the nations.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping that women will be raised up as signs of the Revelation among the nations; widens the education movement.

selected.text: He counseleth you with that which draweth you nigh unto God, the Lord of all worlds - with trustworthiness, religious devotion, chastity and fidelity, and with that through which the essence of justice may be made manifest in the contingent world.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling trustworthiness, devotion, chastity and fidelity through which the essence of justice appears; links trust and justice.

selected.text: Therefore, O ye who are intoxicated with the wine of the divine covenant and O ye who are lovers of the countenance of Truth, strive to become the dawning-places of the signs of divine unity and the rising-points of the lights of the Glorious Lord.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to the lovers of Truth to become dawning-places of the signs of divine unity; draws the closing toward unity.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to rest not a moment but strive, work and serve night and day; an image of sustained effort.

selected.text: O my handmaiden! Rejoice in My mention, for it is better for thee than every deed and every wise command. Beware lest the veils of women hold thee back from the Lord of Names, or the deeds of the idolaters frighten thee from this clear announcement.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh warning a handmaiden not to let the veils of women or the deeds of idolaters hold her back; counsel to a woman in her circumstances.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a recipient speak His praise with complete humility; joins utterance and lowliness.

selected.text: For today it is binding and obligatory upon everyone, whether female or male, that their deeds be in accordance with the divine good-pleasure. The Truth has, in most of His Tablets, commanded His maidservants and servants to perform praiseworthy deeds
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh making praiseworthy deeds binding on every woman and man; extends the call to deeds to all believers.

selected.text: O friends! Listen with the ear of the soul to the counsels and admonitions of the Ancient Beauty. As much as you are able, hurt no one's feelings and sadden no heart. Be the cause of joy to hearts and the source of gladness to the world of humanity
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to hurt no one’s feelings, sadden no heart and be a source of joy; a clear statement of gentle conduct.

selected.text: O my beloved! Arise from thy couch, stand up from thy resting place, and strive with utmost endeavor and consummate wisdom which cannot be surpassed to spread the divine fragrances until the horizons are perfumed and heedlessness and hypocrisy vanish.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding a beloved arise from his couch and spread the divine fragrances with consummate wisdom; joins zeal and wisdom.

selected.text: It is time for the friends to free themselves from every thought and occupy themselves with guiding the seekers and directing the lost. If they do this, the rays of the manifest light will, in a brief time, illuminate and brighten the face of the earth.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá urging the friends to free themselves from every thought and guide the seekers, promising the earth’s illumination; turns learning outward.

selected.text: O friends! Reflect upon the proof of the All-Merciful and deprive not yourselves of the eternal realms for the sake of ephemeral days. Cling ye to the cord of the Cause with such firmness that the entire world shall be powerless to separate you from it.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends cling to the Cause so firmly that the whole world cannot separate them; a strong image of firmness.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to strive while time remains and opportunity exists; states the value of time directly.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá rebuking laziness and coldness, since until one burns one cannot become a candle; a memorable image of fervour.
